A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TRUST-VL work. All main-text and appendix material is available for comparison, including readable tables, diagrams, plots, and case studies. Content relocated between versions can be matched.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark evaluations, model ablations, joint-training experiments, evidence-noise robustness tests, and qualitative model comparisons.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and additionally quantifies the instruction-quality inspection outcome.

M1.justification: The backbone, QAVA attention mechanism, evidence retrieval, structured reasoning, and three-stage training remain the same. Redrawn diagrams and expanded construction explanations do not establish a changed procedure; manual inspection and filtering already appeared in v1 Appendix F.

E1.justification: Training sources and evaluation coverage are retained, including the seven principal benchmarks and DGM4-All. The task-specific comparisons and mixed-distortion case highlighted in v2 already appeared in v1's appendices.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged. In particular, LVLM4FV, HAMMER, and SNIFFER in v2 Table 4 already appeared in v1 Table 8. The main comparison and MMD-Agent backbone comparisons also retain their methods.

E3.justification: Reported training stages, budgets, evaluation class counts, accuracy/macro-F1 metrics, and the 60K-sample joint-training control match. Removed audit-size and held-out-test disclosures do not establish changed experimental settings.

E4.justification: The component ablations, backbone-size analysis, joint-training heatmap, QAVA-token sweep, alternative-backbone experiment, incorrect-evidence tests, and case studies are retained. V2 Figure 9 relocates v1 Figure 12 rather than adding a case study.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The newly reported 98.5% inspection pass rate is a point result from an existing inspection process, not a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: V2 Section 3.2 reports a 98.5% instruction-inspection pass rate, replacing v1 Appendix F's qualitative statement that most responses complied. All matched performance tables and plots retain their values. The QAVA discussion corrects the 72.79% to 88.50% example from Factify2 to DGM4-Face, while Figure 4(c) removes four visual-forgery subtype percentages in favor of their aggregate.

T1.justification: Neither version introduces formal propositions or proofs. Evidence-retrieval notation remains unchanged, and the relocated reasoning taxonomy retains its definitions.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution statements retain the same claims about unified detection, QAVA, the 198K instruction dataset, state-of-the-art performance, generalization, and interpretability. The shortened conclusion does not materially change their scope.

C2.justification: V2 Section 4.1 newly attributes strong Factify2 performance to the underlying LLM's handling of long textual context and evidence reasoning. Appendix D adds that evidence-based reasoning is not beneficial for visual-artifact judgments and explains task-dependent reasoning paths. The limitations paragraph remains unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 makes training-source mappings more explicit, but removes v1's specification of 200 inspected samples per dataset, the explicit Factify2 held-out/no-leakage statement, and visual-forgery subtype proportions. Core architecture details, hyperparameters, checkpoints, hardware, and project-access information are retained.

R1.justification: The reference list and substantive related-work positioning are unchanged. The contrast between a jointly optimized unified VLM and loosely connected multi-agent approaches remains the same.

P1.justification: V2 substantially reorganizes the exposition: dataset construction and training become separate subsections, taxonomy and inspection material move into the method section, and task-specific comparisons and a complex case move into the main evaluation. Method, ablation, case-study, and conclusion passages are extensively rewritten, with corresponding appendix consolidation.

P2.justification: Figures 3–5 are substantially redesigned, including simplified architecture/training diagrams and a restructured reasoning-construction figure whose distribution chart becomes a compact statistical display. The taxonomy table, task-specific comparison table, and complex case figure move into the main text. The evaluation-distribution table is also reformatted.

improvement.justification: V2 modestly improves readability through clearer Figures 3–5, better separation of construction and training, and main-text placement of important explanatory material and comparisons. It also corrects the QAVA dataset attribution. These gains are tempered by lost reproducibility details, particularly the inspection sample size and explicit Factify2 split statement; the benchmark evidence itself is unchanged.
